title.zh: 让善意预期与事实核对一起保留
title.en: Keep good-faith expectations alongside factual checks

paragraphs.zh: 回到上面的普通误会，分开记下自己最初的预期、实际知道的经过和仍未确认的原因。例如，可以愿意听解释，同时还要核对共同约定有没有落实。若已经听到解释，再看它补充了什么、哪些问题仍然开放；没有解释也不用替对方补出一个。复盘让期待和证据各有位置，不要求继续交往、提供帮助或原谅谁，也不需要通过改变均分证明自己更善良。
paragraphs.en: Return to the ordinary misunderstanding above and separate your initial expectation, known events and unconfirmed causes. You can be willing to hear an explanation while still checking whether an agreement was fulfilled. If an explanation was given, note what it clarified and what remains open; do not supply one on the other person’s behalf. This gives expectations and evidence their own place without requiring continued contact, help, forgiveness or a changed mean as proof of goodness.

title.zh: 从一个普通互动交换看法

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“假设活动安排出了一个小误会，哪些经过需要先核对，哪些原因还不知道？”先谈情境中的事实、表达与选择，不把回答当作善良程度或是否值得信任的考试。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “If a small misunderstanding occurred in an activity arrangement, which events would need checking and which causes would remain unknown?” Discuss the facts, wording and choices in the situation rather than test goodness or trustworthiness.

title.zh: 把倾听、认同与可用时间分开说明
title.en: Distinguish listening, agreement and available time

paragraphs.zh: 沿用上面的兴趣分享，挑出一个愿意听懂的具体观点，再写下自己赞同、不同意和暂时不清楚的部分。可以尊重表达者，同时核对一项说法，也可以因时间有限暂停谈话。若交流仍在继续，可以复述自己听到的一个意思，再问是否理解准确；对方不愿继续时就停下。复盘关注具体交流，不用欣赏多少人或听了多久来证明个体价值，也不把分数当作倾听效果的保证。
paragraphs.en: For the interest-sharing example, choose a specific view you wanted to understand and separate agreement, disagreement and uncertainty. You can respect the speaker while checking a claim, or pause because time is limited. If the conversation is continuing, restate one point you heard and ask whether you understood it correctly; stop if the other person does not want to continue. Review the exchange without counting admiration or listening time as proof of worth, or treating a score as a guarantee of effective listening.

title.zh: 从一个普通互动交换看法

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“假设朋友分享一个你不完全赞同的兴趣观点，你会怎样表示听懂了哪部分、还有哪里想问？”先谈情境中的事实、表达与选择，不把回答当作善良程度或是否值得信任的考试。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “If a friend shared an interest-related view you did not fully agree with, how would you say what you understood and what you would still ask about?” Discuss the facts, wording and choices in the situation rather than test goodness or trustworthiness.

title.zh: 把请求的目的、范围与拒绝空间说清
title.en: Clarify a request’s aim, scope and room to decline

paragraphs.zh: 回看上面的普通求助，把自己的目标、希望对方做的具体部分、时间要求和是否可以拒绝分别写清。若原先表达不够明确，可在本来就需要讨论时补充一项遗漏，而不是重复测试对方愿不愿意帮忙。例如，“我想整理这些资料，你愿意只帮我核对这一页吗？没时间也可以。”明确目标不等于利用别人；是否尊重选择，要看实际说了什么、怎样回应，而不由这次自报评分认证。
paragraphs.en: Revisit the ordinary request by specifying your aim, the particular help sought, timing and room to decline. If something was unclear, add one missing detail when discussion is already needed rather than repeatedly testing willingness. For example: “I want to organise these materials. Would you check just this page? It is fine if you have no time.” Stating a goal is not itself using someone. Respect for choice depends on the actual request and response rather than certification by self-report ratings.

title.zh: 从一个普通互动交换看法

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“假设你希望别人帮忙核对一页资料，怎样说清目的、范围，并让拒绝也容易表达？”先谈情境中的事实、表达与选择，不把回答当作善良程度或是否值得信任的考试。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “If you wanted someone to check one page of materials, how would you state the aim and scope while making refusal easy to express?” Discuss the facts, wording and choices in the situation rather than test goodness or trustworthiness.
